newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy mourns loss of movie legend Mastroianni.
newsitem.headline: Italy mourns loss of movie legend Mastroianni.

text.p: Italy and the world cinema plunged into mourning for the death of movie legend Marcello Mastroianni, the quintessential Latin Lover who captured the hearts of millions.
Mastroianni died at his home in Paris on Thursday, aged 72. Friends said he had been suffering from cancer.
"A big part of me and of my youth has gone," said Italian actress Sophia Loren, with whom Mastroianni built an inimitable screen partnership in 12 of his best-known films.
"I thank God for having known someone like him," Loren's sister Maria Scicolone, quoted her as saying from Paris.

Rome's Trevi Fountain, the setting for one of Mastroianni's most memorable cinematic scenes in Federico Fellini's "La Dolce Vita", was swathed in black and stopped flowing as tributes poured in to one of the movie world's most charismatic figures.
"Farewell Marcello" Italian state television RAI said simply at the start of a news broadcast almost entirely taken over by the news, and illustrated with clips from some of his 160 films.

Mastroianni's body was due to be returned to Italy on Friday after a service in Paris. Officials said he would lie in state at Rome's city hall on the Capitoline Hill from Saturday afternoon until his funeral in Rome on Sunday.
Colleagues said Mastroianni was warm, self-deprecating, ironic -- and never played the star.

"He was a great actor because he was always himself," said Anita Ekberg, the voluptuous Swedish blonde whose romp with Mastroianni in the waters of the Trevi Fountain in "La Dolce Vita" in 1960 is one of cinema's indelible images.
In a surreal scene evocative of Fellini's work, the city of Rome switched off the water, turned out the fountain's lights and unfurled two black cloth banners over the Baroque monument.
Mastroianni's widow, Flora Carabella, broke down in tears as a musician played the eerie theme of Fellini's "8 1/2", one of Marcello's own favourite films, on a recorder. Bells tolled.
The mayor of Fontana Liri, where Mastroianni was born on September 24, 1924, declared Friday a day of mourning and said flags would fly at half mast.
President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro said in a telegram of condolence to Mastroianni's widow that Italians had lost an ambassador of culture and "a man they loved and admired".
Mastroianni, who said he never liked the Latin Lover tag, refused to divorce Flora despite many affairs including one with French actress Catherine Deneuve, who was with him when he died.
Also present were Mastroianni's two daughters -- Barbara, from his marriage, and Chiara, from his liaison with Deneuve.
"I haven't always been loyal," he admitted in an interview last year, in which he said he said he hated the idea of death.
"But between love and work, I've been very lucky. Maybe the secret is that I've loved life."
